gap.behavioural_impact: In Edison the EDOPro card destroys every 'Blaze Accelerator' card you control instead of a single face-up one, and skips the board wipe and the Token entirely whenever that destruction fails, where the period card wiped the field regardless. Round 037 (2026-09-29): withdrawn as a difference on period rulings: Era: the field wipe and the Token do not depend on the Blaze Accelerator destruction succeeding; modern: 'and if you do' / 'then' chain them. Case A: the Blaze Accelerator is removed from the field in response. (review notes).

review.notes:
Only two English versions: v0 (FOTB-EN039, 2007-05-16), the text in force at the Edison snapshot, and v1 (SGX1-ENH16, 2022-03-17); no intermediate printings, so the whole rewrite lands in one dated transition. Pinned BabelCDB text matches v1 exactly (ratio 1.0). upstream_implementations is empty. 'destroy as many monsters on the field as possible' is PSCT phrasing of 'destroy all monsters on the field' and is not counted as a delta; the Token's printed statline is unchanged apart from Pyro-Type / Pyro and LEVEL / Level. The card is not on EdisonFormat.com's functional errata page, so the verdict rests on the printed lineage - but the one-versus-all and face-up-versus-any deltas are explicit in the text rather than inferred from PSCT convention, which makes this the least ambiguous functional call in the batch.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Wild Fire). A period ruling in force contradicts part of the claim, which is withdrawn as a difference: Era: the field wipe and the Token do not depend on the Blaze Accelerator destruction succeeding; modern: 'and if you do' / 'then' chain them. Case A: the Blaze Accelerator is removed from the field in response. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_uz page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): ""Blaze Accelerator" is destroyed when "Wild Fire" resolves. If an effect is chained that removes "Blaze Accelerator" from the field, "Wild Fire's" effect disappears and you can attack that turn." Konami TCG Card FAQ default_uz page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "If there are no monsters on the field when "Wild Fire" resolves, you cannot Special Summon any Tokens, but you can declare an attack that turn." The transition stays functional on what remains, d1, d2, d4. Verdicts: [event] d1 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d2 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d4 unresolved at Edison, unresolved at Tengu; d3 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Functional erratum on two counts. The FOTB-EN039 text destroys 'a face-up "Blaze Accelerator" card you control' - exactly one card, and only a face-up one - while the modern text destroys 'all "Blaze Accelerator" cards you control', face-down Set copies included, so controlling both 'Blaze Accelerator' and 'Tri-Blaze Accelerator' now costs you both. And the period text then destroyed all monsters on the field and Summoned the Token unconditionally, whereas the modern text makes the field wipe and the Token depend on that first destruction succeeding ('and if you do, destroy as many monsters on the field as possible, then, Special Summon 1 "Wild Fire Token"'). The 500 LP payment stays an activation cost and the attack restriction is unchanged in substance."

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the errata'd text (SGX1-ENH16, Speed Duel GX: Duel Academy Box)

event.historical_text: Pay 500 Life Points. Destroy a face-up "Blaze Accelerator" card you control and destroy all monsters on the field. Then, Special Summon 1 "Wild Fire Token" (Pyro-Type/FIRE/LEVEL 3/ATK 1000/DEF 1000) in Attack Position. Also, you cannot declare an attack this turn.
event.modern_text: Pay 500 LP; destroy all "Blaze Accelerator" cards you control, and if you do, destroy as many monsters on the field as possible, then, Special Summon 1 "Wild Fire Token" (Pyro/FIRE/Level 3/ATK 1000/DEF 1000) in Attack Position. Your monsters cannot attack the turn you activate this card.
event.summary: Functional erratum, narrowed by round 037 (2026-09-29) to what no period ruling contradicts: (d1) Era: destroys one face-up "Blaze Accelerator" card you control; modern: destroys all "Blaze Accelerator" cards you control (so with both Blaze Accelerator and Tri-Blaze Accelerator out, the modern card destroys both). (d2) Era: only a face-up "Blaze Accelerator" card is destroyed; modern: all "Blaze Accelerator" cards you control including face-down Set copies. (d4) Same as d3 but Case B: the Blaze Accelerator is still on the field yet its destruction fails (prevented or negated); era: wipe and Token still happen; modern: they do not. Withdrawn as a difference: Era: the field wipe and the Token do not depend on the Blaze Accelerator destruction succeeding; modern: 'and if you do' / 'then' chain them. Case A: the Blaze Accelerator is removed from the field in response. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_uz page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): ""Blaze Accelerator" is destroyed when "Wild Fire" resolves. If an effect is chained that removes "Blaze Accelerator" from the field, "Wild Fire's" effect disappears and you can attack that turn."
